research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10842 at 24 FR 8249 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed October 6, 1959; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the October 10, 1959 issue. The register title is Creating a Board of Inquiry To Report on Certain Labor Disputes Affecting the Maritime Industry.  Inventory confirmed: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 1231 to 2827 of the held text, which runs from the recitals through the continuation sentence and the signing block. The text layer of this page is partly garbled, so no order text is quoted here beyond Executive Order 12553. Content: a recital of a labor dispute in the maritime industry; under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 the order creates a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues, gives the Board the powers and duties of Title II of the Act, directs a report to the President under section 206 by a stated date, and continues the Board in existence after its report to perform other functions required under the Act until the President terminates it. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10842 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry, extracted separately and matched by position, reads creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime industry). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). The report date is a deadline and not an end (owner ruling of 2026-10-21, report deadline). The order says the Board continues after its report until the President terminates it; no held source shows a presidential termination of this Board and no board report is held, so no functionally-spent date is recorded and the revocation is the first end shown. Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a report deadline and a continuation until presidential termination, neither of which is an end shown in a held source; the packet's number search finds no held text citing this order; the dossier chain names only Executive Order 12553. Prior research: the dossier shows no canonical prior claim and no conflicting versions.
